title: The Rich Man and His Ring (മലയാളം)
summary: A foolish nobleman searches for a lost ring under a palace lamp instead of in his bedroom. Birbal uses the incident to satirize human escapism. [ML]
keywords: the rich man and his ring
full_text:
Late one evening, Emperor Akbar and Birbal were walking through the outer courtyard of the Agra palace when they noticed a wealthy nobleman, Mirza Asad, on his hands and knees beneath a brightly glowing oil street lamp, frantically sifting through pebbles and dust.

Akbar stopped: 'Mirza Asad, what are you doing in the dirt at this late hour?'

Asad looked up, sweating: 'Your Majesty, I have lost my priceless ruby ring, a family heirloom worth ten thousand rupees! I am searching for it!'

Akbar, feeling generous, knelt down with Birbal and helped the nobleman search. For nearly an hour, the Emperor, the minister, and the noble combed through every inch of dust beneath the lantern. The ring was nowhere to be found.

Birbal wiped his hands and asked: 'Mirza Asad, are you certain you dropped the ring right here beneath this lamp?'

Asad replied innocently: 'Oh no, Raja Birbal! I dropped it inside my dark bedroom, three corridors away inside the palace!'

Akbar jumped to his feet in disbelief: 'You dropped it in your bedroom? Then why in heaven's name are you searching for it out here in the courtyard?'

Asad blinked in surprise: 'Because it was pitch black in my bedroom, Sire, and there is such wonderful, bright light out here under this courtyard street lamp!'

Akbar stared in stunned silence, then burst into a roar of exasperated laughter.

Birbal turned to the Emperor and said with profound philosophical humor:

'Do not mock him too harshly, Your Majesty. Most of humanity behaves exactly like Mirza Asad!

'When men lose their inner peace, their health, or their moral character inside the quiet chambers of their own hearts, they never search for it within themselves where it was lost, because self-examination is dark and difficult!

'Instead, they run out into the brightly lit courtyards of the world—chasing wealth, fame, flattery, and sensual pleasures—hoping to find their lost peace where the lights are bright, even though it was never dropped there!'

Akbar was captivated by the brilliant metaphor. He ordered a lantern brought to Mirza Asad's bedroom, where the ring was promptly found under a cushion, and thanked Birbal for illuminating a profound spiritual truth.
